title: Direct destination selector
description:
How the SENDER addressed the message, which is what enters the deduplication key — not the endpoint the receiver ultimately resolved. The distinction is load-bearing: keying on the resolved endpoint would let a profile's default change mid-TTL and turn one logical message into two deliveries (ADR-0019).

On the wire this is carried by `destination_endpoint_len`: zero means Default, non-zero means Explicit. Here it is the logical form used in dedup keys and diagnostics.

oneOf.description: The sender omitted the endpoint, asking for the receiver's configured default_direct_endpoint. Never fan-out, and never a wildcard.
